content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E029 (Jesus Cooke) requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- Note 1 (HR-ish): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommends write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Payroll Specialist (not verified), employment type contractor, security training basic, recommends read. Comment says Security DB shows contractor, not full-time as previously noted.

The Security agent has looked up in their own database: contractor, basic security training. Contractors without advanced training max out at read. So the maximum for this employee is read (since contractor, no advanced training, never admin; contractor read or write if advanced training; here basic training so read max).

Requested level: write. Above maximum (read). Grant maximum: read.

Security note claims the HR note was wrong. The security agent looked up employment type in own database. HR agent also looked up in own database. There's a conflict. The approver must decide. The security note states explicitly the discrepancy and recommends read. Given policy says contractors without advanced training max at read, and the security DB shows contractor/basic, grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.
